item.title: Incarico di ricerca: Compatible and structure-preserving discretizations of Hamiltonian PDE systems (Univ. TRENTO)
item.description:
Deadline: 2026-12-18 12:00
Institution: Univ. TRENTO, Trento
Field: Mathematics and computer science / 01/MATH-05 Analisi numerica

The objective of this research project is to develop new compatible and structure-preserving schemes for Hamiltonian PDE systems that originate from the SHTC / GENERIC frameworks. The new methods should discretize the original Lie-Poisson gradient-flow system in a compatible manner and ensure at the same time semi-discrete or fully-discrete total energy conservation as well as a provable entropy inequality. For certain PDE systems involutions like the divergence-free property of the magnetic field must be guaranteed.

item.title: Incarico di ricerca: Asymptotic behaviors of microscopic and nonlocal interactions (Univ. NAPOLI)
item.description:
Deadline: 2026-12-21 09:00
Institution: Univ. NAPOLI, Napoli
Field: Mathematics and computer science / 01/MATH-03 Analisi matematica, probabilità e statistica matematica

Microscopic and nonlocal interactions are common features in Biology, Social Sciences, and Materials Science, and often give rise to relevant macroscopic phenomena. The aim of the research fellowship is to develop effective models for multi-agent systems and Materials Science, starting from microscopic considerations. The research plan addresses the following three areas: (1) Multi-agent-based optimization; (2) Homogenization and Free Discontinuity; (3) Nonlocal approach to Free Discontinuity.

The research project focuses on the design and development of persuasive video games aimed at changing players’ real-world behaviors. To this end, it will employ Artificial Intelligence methods and technologies capable of adapting aspects of the game to individual players, as well as generative AI (LLMs) that uses natural language for persuasive purposes. Particular attention will also be paid to designing and evaluating the player experience, with a specific focus on the effects of gameplay on players’ behavior and the potential influence of aspects of the “relationship” between players and LLMs (e.g., humanization and alliance) on the interaction. item.description:

Institution: ROMA "Tor Vergata", Roma
Field: Mathematics and computer science / 01/MATH-04 Fisica matematica

The aim is to study the dynamics of the N-body problem in Celestial Mechanics using analytical and computational methods with particular reference to the dynamics around resonances and stability problems. To this end, methods from perturbation theory, chaos indicators, machine learning techniques, and high-performance computing methodologies will be used. The numerical simulations will be carried out using integrators for the N-body problem, and by developing programs and algorithms using programming languages such as Mathematica, Matlab, Python, C/C++. The research activity aims to define multi-level software engineering methods for the design, implementation, and analysis of multi-agent systems (MAS), in which the behaviour of individual agents (micro level) must predictably realise collective goals and properties (macro level).
